why: The signs drawn in the 3D garden are in Spanish in A ("Julio", "Agosto", "de · 13 jul") but in English in B ("July", "August", "de · 13 Jul", which also mixes Spanish "de" with English "Jul"), and world text must be in the language the learner studies.

The signs in the 3D garden show the month names in Spanish in B ("Julio", "Agosto", "13 jul"), but in English in A ("July", "August", "13 Jul"), and in-world text must be in the language the learner studies.
I found no visible difference between A and B in any of the three moments (top bar, help text, buttons, icons and the 3D garden all match).
Each A-n matches its B-n in every part I compared (top bar, hint box, garden scene, labels drawn in the world, the action button, Next plant and Finish today's practice), so no difference matters.

B turns the Colors, Growing plants and Sound settings into loose pills styled exactly like the page's action buttons (the chosen one is the same cream pill as "Make demo learner and open the garden", with no check mark), so choices look like actions and their state is shown by fill alone, while A uses a checked segmented control and on/off toggles.

A shows the selected Colors/Growing plants/Sound option only by a cream fill on pills that look like the primary action button (and marks "Show plants growing" as on while saying the plants do not move), while B uses a segmented control with a check mark and real toggles, including a disabled growth toggle that says why it is off.

B draws the Colors, Growing plants and Sound choices as full-width pill buttons like the Download actions, marks the selected one only by a dark fill, and shows "Show plants growing" selected while its text says the plants do not move; A uses a checkmarked list and switches whose state is clear and matches the text.

In A the Colors, Growing plants and Sound settings are full-width pill buttons that look the same as the action buttons (Download, Send me a code) and show the chosen one only by a black fill, and A even marks "Show plants growing" as chosen while its text says the plants do not move; B uses a checkmarked list and labelled toggles whose state is clear, with the motion toggle shown off and disabled to match its text.

B adds a joke line to every plant card ("It remembers you too.", "A good word. Very sure of itself."), which makes the card taller and puts a playful aside in the way of learning, while A keeps the card plain and useful.
A's plant card adds a joke line under the facts ("It remembers you too.", "A good word. Very sure of itself."), an aside that breaks the plain-text rule, while B's card shows only the useful facts.

B adds a joking aside line to the plant card ("It remembers you too.", "A good word. Very sure of itself."), which breaks the plain-text rule and makes the card taller so it covers part of the yellow arrow pointing at the plant.

A adds jokey aside lines to the plant card ("It remembers you too.", "A good word. Very sure of itself."), which breaks the plain-text, no-jokes rule and makes the card taller so it hides the pointer arrow and more of the garden.

B moves the learner over the stile with a "Climb over the stile" button press and no walking, then jumps them back to the stile top on the next W press, which breaks the rule that a button never moves you; in A you climb the stile by walking with W.

In A the "Climb over the stile" button carries the learner off to the far hilltop and then W snaps them back onto the stile (a travel button plus a teleport, both against the physical-garden rule), while in B you simply walk up and over the stile with W; B's own flaw, the camera sinking into the edge hedge in B-3/B-4, is smaller.

In B a "Climb over the stile" button carries you over the fence and one W press puts you back on the garden side, which breaks the no-travel-button and no-teleport rules; A lets you walk over the steps (its one flaw is the camera ending up inside the bramble hedge in A-3/A-4).

A crosses the stile with a "Climb over the stile" button, a button that moves the learner, which the rules forbid; it also leaves them stuck for 12 s in an empty flat meadow and then snaps them back onto the stile, while B lets the learner walk over the stile (B's camera clipping into the bramble hedge in B-3/B-4 is a real bug, but a smaller one).

B draws the wrong-answer "x" and the "Correct answer: Lo" line in a darker red that reads clearly on the beige page (A's bright orange-red has weak contrast), and its "Enter" hint on the Next button is crisper too.

B draws the wrong-answer text ("Correct answer: Lo" and the typed "x") in a lighter orange-red with weaker contrast on the beige background, and its "Enter" keycap on the Next button is dimmer grey, while A keeps both in darker, more readable colours.
B draws the wrong "x" and the "Correct answer: Lo" line in a darker red (and its Enter hint lighter), so the text has better contrast than A's light orange-red on the beige and pink backgrounds.
